mcp.intro: Expose the connections you choose below to an AI coding tool (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Antigravity, Codex, …) over the Model Context Protocol — opt-in per connection, with a per-connection write policy (read-only by default).
mcp.sharedIdsHint: A connection published by a shared origin keeps the same id on every machine, so a snippet built from shared connections works for the whole team as-is.
mcp.bulkPolicyNoop: They were already set to that
mcp.bulkPolicyFullBody: Full access lets an AI client change data AND schema on these connections — CREATE, ALTER, DROP included. Every write is recorded in the app's MCP audit log, but nothing asks again at the time.
mcp.unavailable: Not found — this build wasn't installed from a packaged release, so the connector isn't bundled.
mcp.noConnections: No saved connections yet — add one first.
mcp.writePolicyHint: Write access is per connection. “Read-only” allows only reads; “Data” allows row changes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE); “Full” also allows schema changes (CREATE/DROP/ALTER). Changes take effect without restarting the AI client. The client still asks you to approve each action, and every write is recorded in mcp-audit.log next to your profiles.
mcp.selectHint: Select at least one connection above.
mcp.fullGuide: Full setup guide (Codex, Claude Desktop, flags, tools)…

about.tagline: Minimal desktop database manager for PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite.
about.tabStateHint: A sibling {{file}} stores the open tabs and schema-tree expansion for each connection.

live.label: Open right now
live.desc: Connections HuginnDB is holding against your servers. Other clients on this machine — IDE data sources, application connection pools, huginndb-mcp sidecars — count against the same server limits.

maxConnections.label: Max connections per server
maxConnections.desc: The whole allowance HuginnDB will spend against one server, shared by every connection and database view that reaches it. A server that needs a different budget is better set on the connection itself, where it also travels to exports and to the MCP connector.

childMaxConnections.label: Max connections per database view
childMaxConnections.desc: Browsing a multi-database server opens a separate pool per database, drawing on the same per-server allowance. Keep this low — it multiplies by the number of databases you open.

maxChildPools.label: Max open database views
maxChildPools.desc: Longest-unused database views are closed past this limit. 0 means unlimited.

childIdleTtl.label: Close idle database views after
childIdleTtl.desc: Seconds a database view may go untouched before its pool is closed. It reopens by itself the next time you use it. 0 disables this.

keepalive.label: Keepalive interval
keepalive.desc: Seconds between liveness pings. The ping holds one connection open per connection so the next click is instant and dropped connections are detected early. 0 turns it off.

connections.footnote: Limits apply when a pool is opened; pools already open keep what they were granted. Reconnect to apply them immediately. When a server's allowance is spent, opening a database view closes the one you used least recently rather than failing.

mcpBridge.label: Share pools with the MCP connector
mcpBridge.desc: Let a running huginndb-mcp sidecar use this app's connections instead of opening its own, so the whole machine shares one budget per server — and its activity appears in the Console as it happens. Opens a token-protected listener on localhost. Off by default.

position.label: Position
position.desc: Corner or edge the stack grows from.

duration.label: Duration
duration.desc: How long a dismissible notification stays. Warnings and file notifications get a multiple of this.

errorsPersist.label: Errors wait to be dismissed
errorsPersist.desc: An error usually carries something to copy, retry or report — and none of that happens in six seconds.

maxVisible.label: Visible at once
maxVisible.desc: The rest collapse behind a counter and go straight to the history.

expandOnHover.label: Expand on hover
expandOnHover.desc: Opens the stack and freezes every timer while the pointer is over it.

density.label: Density
density.desc: Compact drops the body line and keeps title plus actions on one row.

historyLimit.label: History entries
historyLimit.desc: Kept in memory by this window only — never written to disk. 0 turns the history off.

showBell.label: Bell in the toolbar
showBell.desc: With it off the history is still kept and still reachable from the command palette.

preview.title: Preview
preview.desc: Fires a real notification, with its timer and its hairline, so the seconds can be judged rather than guessed.

1_18_0.tagline: A notification system built for the app, full view management over the MCP connector, and a project-wide performance and reliability pass.

notifications.title: A notification system of its own
notifications.body: Every toast is now rendered by HuginnDB itself, not the library's stock defaults — a themed card, duplicate notifications collapsed into one with a counter, a history behind a bell in the toolbar, and a progress card for imports and exports that outlive the dialog that started them.

mcpViews.title: Views over the MCP connector: read, edit and delete
mcpViews.body: An AI client can now read a view's definition, create or redefine one, and drop it, on all five drivers — including MongoDB's stored aggregation pipelines. Same write policy as any other DDL change: a connection needs full write access.

performance.title: Internal: a faster, more reliable app under the hood
performance.body: Fixed a multi-second launch freeze caused by re-hashing every shared-origin secret on the main thread, and a SQL Server bug that hung the schema explorer forever loading columns. A project-wide pass also removed duplicated logic across the Rust backend and the frontend — same behavior, less code to drift.

bugFixes.title: A round of issue and bug fixes
bugFixes.body: Dropping a MongoDB "view" whose name matched a real collection could wipe every document in it — now refused. Blank-named MongoDB indexes, bulk updates on MySQL BIT columns, and a dozen smaller inconsistencies (locale formatting, import numbering, missing translations) are fixed too.

docsSections.title: The documentation viewer now has sections
docsSections.body: Each guide opens on a cover with a card per section, the sidebar is a tree derived straight from the markdown, and in-document links actually jump to their target now.

1_17_0.tagline: Your editor now understands JSON Schemas — and a runaway query can no longer take down the app.

jsonSchemas.title: A JSON Schema library, bound to your columns
jsonSchemas.body: Keep a library of named schemas and bind each one to a column (by connection, database, table and column, with globs and a most-specific-wins cascade). A bound column gets real completion, enum suggestions, hover documentation and underlined violations in the cell editor — in the modal and the docked panel, on every driver including MongoDB and SQL Server. "Create from this value" drafts one from the document you're already looking at. Validation never blocks a save: the database stays the authority.

querySafety.title: A runaway SELECT can no longer crash the app
querySafety.body: A hand-typed query with no LIMIT/TOP over a huge table used to buffer the entire result in memory and could take the whole app down with an out-of-memory crash. Every ad-hoc read path now caps itself at 50,000 rows and shows a "truncated" badge instead, and the data grid renders rows through a real virtualizer rather than one DOM row per result.

originEnvironments.title: Shared origins can now sync a whole environment
originEnvironments.body: Point an origin at an environment export instead of a plain profile bundle and it keeps a read-only mirror environment in sync on every pull — created on first sync, refreshed after, and reported as vanished (never silently deleted) if the file disappears.

importProgress.title: Bulk imports get a progress bar and one-click conflict resolution
importProgress.body: The profile/environment import dialogs now show "N of total" while a large import runs off the main thread, and "Mark all as: Rename/Overwrite/Skip" resolves a whole conflict list at once instead of one row at a time.

columnReorder.title: Reorder columns in the MySQL structure editor
columnReorder.body: Move a column up or down without dropping and re-adding it — MySQL's MODIFY COLUMN / ADD COLUMN … FIRST|AFTER makes this possible; the other drivers don't have an equivalent ALTER.

1_16_0.tagline: MongoDB gets a real editing surface — a Compass-style aggregation editor for views and a full index manager — plus a connection-reliability fix for long-idle multi-database sessions, and a visual refresh: a new logo and light/dark pairs for every built-in theme.

mongoAggregation.title: Edit MongoDB views with a Compass-style aggregation editor
mongoAggregation.body: "New aggregation…" on any collection opens a scratch pipeline, and "Edit pipeline…" on any view loads its stored one — both in a Stages view (one card per stage, its own sample output) or a single Text editor, with export as a mongosh call, a bare pipeline, or a db.createView(…) snippet. $out and $merge are refused before they ever reach the server.

mongoIndexes.title: A real index manager for MongoDB
mongoIndexes.body: "Indexes…" on any collection opens the real catalogue — create, hide, replace and drop — showing each index's size and how many operations it's served since the counter was last reset, so you can spot the ones nobody queries. Editing is a drop plus a create, since MongoDB can't alter an index in place.

connectionReliability.title: Multi-database connections stay usable after sitting idle
connectionReliability.body: A server-style connection (Postgres/MySQL/SQL Server) used to stop browsing a database after a few idle minutes even though the tree still showed it connected — the reaped child pool behind it is now reopened transparently on the next click. The huginndb-mcp connector also stopped misreporting a legitimate null result as an empty reply.

brandIdentity.title: A real brand identity, not just an icon
brandIdentity.body: The old raven/rune mark is gone — a new comic logo now leads the About card, the launch splash, and the medallion every empty screen shares (connections tree, console, saved queries, an empty result set), each with its own glyph as a corner badge. Every installer icon, from the Windows taskbar down to Android/iOS, was regenerated from it, and the dev tab finally has a favicon.

themePairs.title: Every built-in theme now has a light/dark twin
themePairs.body: Summer Dark and Neon Light join the roster, and High Contrast now works in both directions — ten themes total, each with a real counterpart instead of stranding you on a HuginnDB default. The 26-colour editor in Preferences → Appearance is also split into four labelled sections (Surfaces, Actions & brand, Status colours, Borders & focus) so related tokens read together.

1_15_0.tagline: Environments get a face of their own, Linux finally gets installers straight off the releases page, and two rough edges — fold state shared where it shouldn't be, and a restart button that went silent — are filed down.

environmentAvatars.title: Give an environment its own image
environmentAvatars.body: The create/rename dialog now takes a custom avatar: pick a file, or drop one on the preview. It replaces the initials everywhere the environment appears — the rail, the workspace picker, the status-bar switcher — which is what finally tells "Cliente A" and "Cliente B" apart at a glance. Whatever you pick is cropped square and downscaled, and it travels inside the environment itself. The rail's label is slightly larger too, and the active one now reads in bold.

linuxBuilds.title: Linux downloads on the releases page
linuxBuilds.body: Every tagged release now attaches an x86_64 .deb and .AppImage next to the Windows installer, so Linux no longer means building from source. The README covers both, including which glibc the AppImage is built against.

independentFolds.title: Folds stay where you left them
independentFolds.body: Collapsing a connection group inside the connections manager no longer reaches behind the dialog and collapses it in the Schema tree as well. Every surface now starts from the same remembered arrangement but folds independently from there, and "remember" still writes through for the next one you open.

restartFeedback.title: "Restart now" shows it heard you
restartFeedback.body: The install button used to keep looking idle and clickable through the whole MCP-sidecar check that runs before an update installs. It now disables itself and shows a spinner the instant you click, and a second click can no longer queue a second install.

1_14_0.tagline: The command palette becomes a real launcher, the window shell reorganizes around an activity bar, environments get their own rail, and themes travel between machines.

paletteLauncher.title: The palette is a real launcher now
paletteLauncher.body: Ctrl/Cmd+K indexes thirteen groups — every preference and shortcut, every doc, open tabs, connections, environments, tables and views across all connected connections, saved queries and history — scored and ranked, with mode prefixes (>, @, #, ?, :) and a "Recently used" section. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P opens it in actions-only mode.

activityBarShell.title: A redesigned window shell
activityBarShell.body: Schema, Saved and Console are no longer draggable dockview panels: Console docks to the bottom, Saved collapses from a right-hand activity bar, and the workspace is a fixed island with its own header. Every panel animates open and closed, and new toggle buttons show or hide each one independently.

environmentRail.title: An environment rail
environmentRail.body: The left activity bar is now a Discord/Teams-style column of environment avatars — initials over each environment's accent colour — replacing the old icon picker. Click one to switch and open Schema in one gesture; right-click for rename/delete.

themeTransfer.title: Import and export themes
themeTransfer.body: Settings → Appearance can now save the active theme to a JSON file and load one back as a brand-new custom theme. A new "Summer" built-in theme joins the set, and environments can carry their own theme override.

columnFit.title: Double-click a column edge to fit it
columnFit.body: The data grid's column resize handle now double-click-fits a column to its widest visible value (Ctrl/Cmd-click fits every column at once), and the toolbar's responsive collapse keeps filters and actions usable on a narrow pane.

1_13_0.tagline: A fifth engine — Microsoft SQL Server — a connection footprint that is finally bounded, visible and yours to set, and a list view that edits on every driver.

sqlServer.title: Microsoft SQL Server
sqlServer.body: The fifth driver: connect (SSH tunnels, named instances, Windows authentication on Windows builds), browse schemas/tables/views/indexes, run T-SQL, and edit, insert, delete and bulk-update rows. The structure editor and .sql export stay read-only for now.

connectionFootprint.title: Far fewer connections
connectionFootprint.body: Browsing a multi-database server no longer opens an unbounded pool per database: they are capped, reused and closed after five minutes idle. Cross-database search stops flooding the server, MongoDB takes the same budget as everyone else, and a "too many connections" error now says so — with what HuginnDB itself is holding.

connectionSettings.title: A budget you set, per server
connectionSettings.body: Settings → Connections shows live how many pools are open and lets you set the allowance for a whole server — shared by every connection and database view reaching it — globally or on a single connection.

listEditor.title: The list view now edits
listEditor.body: Double-click a value to edit it in place, fold and unfold nested objects and arrays, and on MongoDB change a field's BSON type, add fields or remove them. It is no longer MongoDB-only: PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite get it too.

mcpPools.title: One budget, MCP included
mcpPools.body: The huginndb-mcp connector can borrow the app's pools instead of opening its own, so however many AI clients are configured the machine keeps one budget per server — and their activity shows up live in the Console.

1_12_1.tagline: Export and import get a proper redesign — connection- and database-level dialogs, plus grid-toolbar shortcuts — alongside a bulk update tool and a reworked structure editor.

exportImport.title: Export/import redesign
exportImport.body: "Export database…" is now a dialog covering one or more databases (and, per database, which tables) into a single combined .sql file; "Import .sql…" previews the statement count and lets multi-DB connections pick a target. The grid toolbar gained its own "Export data" (full table or query results) and, for MongoDB, "Import JSON…".

bulkUpdate.title: Bulk update
bulkUpdate.body: Update every row/document matching a filter in one round trip, for all four drivers — reuses the grid's advanced-filter builder for the match side and previews the exact statement before running.

structureEditor.title: Categorised type picker
structureEditor.body: The structure editor's column type combo is now grouped by category (Integers/Real/Text/Date & time/Binary/Other) with its own length/precision field and MySQL unsigned/zerofill checkboxes, plus a redesigned columns table matching the app's own grid look.

tableRename.title: Renaming a table works again
tableRename.body: The Name field is editable when editing a table, and applying a rename updates every open tab's title instead of leaving the old name showing.

1_12_0.tagline: Environments group your connections into named, switchable sessions — with shared origins to sync them across a team, connections now living in the schema tree, and a redesigned query run experience.

environments.title: Environments
environments.body: A new level above connections: a named set of connections with its own tabs, pane layout and reconnect behaviour, switchable from a topbar selector — one environment per client instead of one window per client.

sharedOrigins.title: Shared origins
sharedOrigins.body: An environment can sync its connections — and their passwords — from a shared config file on the network, so joining a team means entering a passphrase once instead of configuring every connection by hand.

connectionsInTree.title: Connections live in the schema tree
connectionsInTree.body: The tree now starts with folders and connections as its top two levels, so opening a second server is a click in the same window instead of a trip through a separate menu.

filterSelected.title: Filter by the selected rows
filterSelected.body: Select rows in the data grid, right-click a column, and filter the rest of the table down to (or excluding) exactly those values — deduplicated, and working on every driver, MongoDB included.

queryFeedback.title: Redesigned query feedback
queryFeedback.body: A live run timer, a bigger default editor/results split, and a searchable query history with a one-click "run again" replace the old bare running/finished label.

neonTheme.title: Neon, a new dark theme
neonTheme.body: A near-black theme built around a signature neon green accent, with cyan/amber/pink picked to match — a fresh coat for anyone tired of the two defaults.

1_11_0.tagline: The app reconnects on launch and opens big tables almost instantly, with a cleaner single-bar grid toolbar, a MongoDB list view and true floating windows.

reconnect.title: Reconnect on launch
reconnect.body: A new General preference (on by default) reopens the connections that were live when you last closed the app — using the credentials already in the OS keychain — restoring the same focused connection, tab and pane layout you left behind.

fastOpen.title: Big tables open almost instantly
fastOpen.body: Rows now render as soon as the query returns instead of waiting on an exact COUNT(*); whole-table totals come from the engine's own statistics as an approximate ~N, so multi-million-row tables no longer stall on open.

toolbar.title: A single, cleaner table toolbar
toolbar.body: The table toolbar is now one Compass-style bar — search grows to fill the width, Insert sits beside it, and pagination, zoom and elapsed time move to the right — dropping the old bottom status strip and the duplicated row count for more grid space.

mongoList.title: MongoDB list view
mongoList.body: MongoDB collections gain a table/list toggle: list mode renders each document as a card with pretty-printed nested objects and arrays, instead of forcing endless horizontal scrolling and one-line JSON blobs in table mode.

floatWindow.title: Float a tab into a real window
floatWindow.body: "Float in new window" now opens a genuine, independent OS window hosting just that one tab — movable anywhere on the desktop — instead of a floating panel trapped inside the workspace pane.

1_10_0.tagline: View editing lands in the schema explorer, alongside fully customizable keyboard shortcuts and quicker grid actions.

viewsEditor.title: Views can now be created, edited and dropped
viewsEditor.body: The schema explorer's new "Edit view…" tab pairs a full Monaco SQL editor with a live preview grid and a read-only DDL pane — no more hand-writing CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW.

betweenFilter.title: A `between` operator in the Advanced Filter
betweenFilter.body: Filter an inclusive range in a single condition — on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and MongoDB — instead of stacking a >= row and a <= row.

shortcuts.title: Customizable keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body: Settings → Shortcuts lets you rebind six actions — open settings, command palette, tab switcher, refresh, run query and the new expand-cell shortcut — with collision checks and a reset-all button.

gridQuickActions.title: Faster data-grid actions
gridQuickActions.body: Click a selected cell to reveal an expand icon for a quick full-value view, and use Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V to copy and paste cell values directly — no more double-clicking just to read.

1_9_0.tagline: Your AI tools can now write to your databases — safely, on your terms, one connection at a time.

mcpWrite.title: MCP connector write-mode
mcpWrite.body: The huginndb-mcp connector, read-only until now, can insert, update and delete rows — and change schema — through your AI tool. New insert_row, update_cell and delete_rows tools, plus writes via run_query.

mcpPolicy.title: Per-connection write policy, with an audit log
mcpPolicy.body: Each connection is read-only by default; raise it to 'data' or 'full' in Settings → MCP, per connection, with changes taking effect immediately. Whole-table UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE are refused, and every write is recorded in mcp-audit.log.

advancedFilter.title: Advanced per-column filter
advancedFilter.body: A new filter button in the table toolbar opens a builder: add conditions per column (contains, starts/ends with, >, <, equals, is null…), all combined with AND and applied on the server. Type-aware, and works across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and MongoDB.

1_8_0.tagline: MongoDB catches up: multi-database connections and the MCP connector both get real driver parity.

security.title: Security panel works on multi-database connections
security.body: Opening the Security tab on a MongoDB connection with no preselected database no longer errors — it now lists users and privileges across the whole cluster.

mcpMongo.title: MCP no longer blocks MongoDB reads
mcpMongo.body: `run_query` used a SQL-only read-only check that rejected every mongosh statement by default. It now recognises MongoDB reads correctly, the same way the desktop query editor already did.

mcpMongoDatabase.title: MCP tools can target a MongoDB database
mcpMongoDatabase.body: list_tables, describe_table, list_indexes, browse_table (schema) and run_query (database) can now target a specific database on a multi-database MongoDB connection — the same thing expanding a database in the explorer does, just from your AI tool.

columnTypes.title: Real column types instead of generic "bson"
columnTypes.body: Query and browse results now show each column's actual BSON type (int, string, date, objectId, …) instead of one generic label — useful for you and for AI tools using the MCP connector.

collectionSize.title: Collection size in the explorer
collectionSize.body: MongoDB collections now show an on-disk size, fetched in a single batched call instead of skipping it.

1_7_0.tagline: Bring your databases to your AI tools — HuginnDB now speaks the Model Context Protocol.

connector.title: MCP connector for AI tools
connector.body: A new headless `huginndb-mcp` server lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients inspect your databases — schema, tables, indexes, sample rows and server info — using the connections you already saved.

safety.title: Read-only and opt-in by design
safety.body: Nothing is exposed until you name a connection, queries are read-only, passwords stay in your OS keychain, and a row cap keeps results in check. See docs/MCP.md to wire up your client.

1_6_0.tagline: A top-to-bottom interface overhaul — the same keyboard-first HuginnDB, sharper in every corner.

design.title: Refined design system
design.body: A consistent colour, type and elevation scale, clearer focus rings, and semantic success / warning tokens that follow your theme.

grid.title: Keyboard-navigable data grid
grid.body: Move the active cell with the arrow keys, select rows with visible checkboxes, and read numbers in aligned tabular figures.

schema.title: Redesigned schema tree
schema.body: The open table is marked so you always know where you are, column types are colour-coded, and rows load behind a subtle skeleton.

editor.title: Sharper query editor & command palette
editor.body: A visible Run button with its shortcut, a flagship cell editor with content-type badges, and a polished command palette with hints.

chrome.title: Clearer status & themed tooltips
chrome.body: Lost connections are unmissable with one-click reconnect, and tooltips across the chrome now match your theme instead of the OS.

origins.title: Shared origins
origins.description: Pull connections from a file on a shared folder. Registered globally, across every environment; HuginnDB only ever reads it.
origins.empty: No shared origins yet. Point one at an exported profiles file on a network share.
origins.removeConfirmConnectionsNote: {{count}} connections it imported stay locally, flagged so you can decide whether to keep or delete them.
origins.removeConfirmEnvironmentsNote: {{count}} environments it published also stay, flagged the same way.
origins.removeConfirmNothingNote: This origin hasn't imported any connections or environments.
origins.passphraseHint: Stored in your OS keychain, never on disk. Leave blank if the file was exported without passwords.

vanished.title: No longer published
vanished.body: "{{origin}}" no longer offers this connection. Keep it as your own, or delete it together with its stored password.
vanished.keepTooltip: Stop tracking the origin and keep the connection locally, editable again.
vanished.retireConfirm:
Delete the connection "{{name}}"?

Its stored password is removed from your keychain too. This cannot be undone.
vanished.mark: "{{origin}}" no longer offers this connection — resolve it from the schema tree or Settings → Shared origins.
vanished.unknownOriginName: a shared origin that no longer exists
vanished.retireAllConfirm: Their stored passwords are removed from your keychain too. This cannot be undone.

vanishedEnvironments.body: "{{origin}}" no longer includes this environment in the shared file. Keep it as your own, or delete it together with its tabs and layout.
vanishedEnvironments.keepTooltip: Stop tracking the origin and keep the environment locally, editable again.
vanishedEnvironments.retireConfirm:
Delete the environment "{{name}}"?

Its tabs and layout are lost. The connections it groups are not deleted.
